A short-pitch winding reduces the induced EMF because kp = sin(βπ/2) < 1. It shortens the coil ends and suppresses the 5th and 7th harmonics, which improves the voltage waveform. There are no contradictions.

explanationIssues: In choiceExplanations[4] and [5], the reason given for rejecting (ウ) 定格容量 is only that it 「とは記述が合わない」 (does not match the wording). That is vague. The uncertainty field also admits the choice was judged only by the definition in the problem text, so this is an open external-check item. Depending on the standard or textbook, an autotransformer's rated capacity may be defined as V2×I2 at rated values (the line capacity), so the basis for calling it wrong is ambiguous. Suggested fix: separate two points. First, the problem says 「二次端子電圧と二次電流との積」 (terminal voltage × current at any operating point), not rated values, so the right term is the general 負荷容量 (line capacity) rather than 定格容量, a rated value. Second, and more decisively, (エ)「多く」 and (オ)「大きい」 are clearly wrong. Make the (エ)(オ) errors the main reason these choices are wrong.

In choiceExplanations[2], the reason for rejecting 自己容量 is only that the product 「負荷容量であり当てはまらない」. It does not explain what 自己容量 means, so the specific reason this choice is wrong is thin. Suggested addition: 自己容量 is the capacity of the series winding, (V2−V1)·I2 (= (V2−V1)/V2 × V2·I2), which is smaller than the load capacity V2·I2. So it is not the product of the secondary terminal voltage and the secondary current.
After the explanation is fixed, remove the reservation in the uncertainty field about judging 自己容量 and 定格容量 only by the problem's wording, or replace it with the verified basis.

The conditions all match: 100 kV·A, 6.3 kV, two identical single-phase transformers, 1 600 W load loss each at rated load, V-V connection, 6.3 kV primary, a 90 kW three-phase balanced load, power factor 1, and the question asks for the total load loss in W across both transformers.
I checked the choices against the original: (1) 324, (2) 432, (3) 648, (4) 864, (5) 1 440. All match.

Recalculation: I = 90×10³/(√3×6 300) ≈ 8.248 A. Rated current = 100×10³/6 300 ≈ 15.87 A. α = 90/(√3×100) ≈ 0.5196, so α² = 0.27. Each transformer's loss is 1 600×0.27 = 432 W, and the total is 864 W. This matches the fixed manifest official answer 4.
